name: Doro Wat (Ethiopian Berbere Chicken Stew)
method: soup/stew pot (deep-brown onions, then simmer chicken ~45 min)
ingredients_verbatim: 3-3 1/2 pounds (1.3-1.6kg) chicken, cut in pieces (or chicken thighs)
3 tablespoons (42g) spiced butter, or more (sub with cooking oil)
4-6 large eggs, soft boiled and shells removed
main_ingredients_note: 'chicken, cut in pieces (or chicken thighs)' - built on chicken thighs; whole-muscle chicken, board-mapped. berbere maps to berbere-seasoning (on board).
why: Verified 567 cal / 8 g carbs / 41 g protein per serving on the source page - mid-band calories and exceptionally low carb. An onion-and-berbere chicken stew finished with hard-boiled eggs; no rice/starch base (served over injera, which we omit). Berbere IS on the board (berbere-seasoning), so this proves a mapped-but-uncommon signature spice. African/Ethiopian entry diversifies an American/Tex-Mex-skewed catalog. Not in the catalog and distinct from the pending yassa/mafe. Spiced butter (niter kibbeh) is flagged - the source itself offers butter/oil (both mapped) as the sub.
